about: The demo's GETs board, invented: the group experiential themes across Juno's, Rowan's and Mabel's PETs. Each GET by its title, with its description, its note, its PETs and sub-PETs, each named by its participant and its title, and the quote ticked for each participant's row of the GET table, in that participant's words. Every PET and sub-PET of the three is named once, under a GET or set aside, a sub-PET set aside where its PET carries it. make_demo.py builds idiograph-gets.json from this and the three cases' boards.

gets.title: Days run to the dog's clock, given a shape or closed in
gets.description: A start and a shape for Mabel and Juno, a closing timetable for Rowan
gets.note: Each day starts when the dog says. Mabel is given a start and a shape, Juno a part of the day that is hers, and Rowan a timetable that closes round him. Convergence in the hour, divergence in what it gives. For Rowan the same early start is fear kept at bay, and the hours have not left him.

members.pet: Out on the lane, where the day becomes hers
Cracking first at twenty past six
Living on her timetable, in the dark at both ends
A dog giving her days a start and a shape

quotes.Juno: And now it is the bit of the day that is mine.
quotes.Rowan: this is all right, this is ours
quotes.Mabel: there wasn't anything to get up for

gets.title: A reason nobody argues with, letting people in or keeping them out
gets.description: Mabel's way back to people, and Rowan's and Juno's way of keeping them off
gets.note: The dog stands between each of them and other people. It opens the estate to Mabel, and for Rowan and Juno it becomes the good reason that keeps others at a distance. The same phrase in two cases, a reason nobody argues with. Mabel's divergence matters: for her the dog is the way back in.

members.pet: Out on the green and among people again
Company in a lonely year, and a world closing in
Five years of it never getting said
Coming home for the dog, and what that says

quotes.Mabel: You wouldn't know it unless you had a dog.
quotes.Rowan: I'd stopped saying yes to things so long ago that people had stopped asking.
quotes.Juno: Five years of it never getting said.

gets.title: A house lit up by a dog, and flat without one
gets.description: Lights on and a welcome at the door, and a house gone flat without
gets.note: The dog makes the house a home with someone in it. Mabel has the lights on again and someone to tell, Juno is wanted at the door and finds the house on standby without her, and Rowan keeps a bowl under the sink. Presence felt rather than seen, in all three. For Juno and Rowan the empty house is part of the theme: two hours of it for her, every day since June for him.

members.pet: Caught going soft, after four years of saying no dog
Wanted at the door, and finding the dog is easier
A house on standby without her
Life in the house again, and someone to tell
Keeping her good name, and her bowl

quotes.Juno: Even when it is quiet it is not empty.
quotes.Mabel: It's like having the lights on.
quotes.Rowan: She wasn't a problem. She was frightened.

gets.title: Losing each other, rehearsed, lived through and written into a will
gets.description: A death rehearsed, a dog given up, a future written into a will
gets.note: Each of them meets the end of the bond in a different tense. Juno rehearses a death still to come, Rowan has given his dog up and cannot settle it, and Mabel expects to go first and has put her dog's future in writing. Three tenses of one loss. Rowan's watchfulness outlasting the dog sits here, the loss lived in the body.

members.pet: Grieving in advance a dog who is snoring at her
Giving her up and not settling what that was
Still listening for other dogs
Making sure Pepper is never left waiting for her

quotes.Juno: So that Saturday was a rehearsal.
quotes.Rowan: If it was settled I wouldn't need to say it every day, would I.

gets.title: Holding on to the dog when keeping her costs something
gets.description: Two hold on at a price, and one lets go and cannot settle it
gets.note: Keeping the dog has a price for each of them. Mabel keeps Pepper against her daughter after a broken wrist, Juno pays in worry and in a regret she has never said, and for Rowan the price grows too high and he gives her up. The divergence is the finding here: two of them hold on and one lets go, and none of them blames the dog.

members.pet: Keeping Pepper after the fall, against her daughter
Unable to keep her, or anyone, safe in that flat
Closest on the night it cost her something
Letting her run, and ageing at the gate
The first year's regret, never said

quotes.Mabel: it felt like she was taking something off me
quotes.Rowan: That wasn't her fault. That was mine.
quotes.Juno: She was not begging. She was just waiting.

set_aside.pet: Goodnight out loud, and two thumps back
A dog between them at half nine
Eating again, and sitting down to it
Told the dog had to go
Telling her what she would have told Dennis
